summary:
Word-visibility map for every installed non-Ex Shree font family is complete. All 24 requested families are installed, and I also measured 7 more: Shree-Ori7-00x, Tam7-00x, Tel7-00x, Kan7-00x, Mal7-00x and the 13- and 7-glyph companion faces Shree-Ban7-00xA and Tel7-00xA. That is 143 faces from C:\Windows\Fonts and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts. Every face has the same (3,1) cmap as its family's representative. A second, independent TTF reader (verify-cmap.js) confirms this with 0 glyph-id mismatches. No two code points share a glyph id; identical outlines are listed per family.

What the first session (01:25-03:15) had already measured, which I checked for completeness and did not redo:
- 6241 test lines (6147 mapped code points, 94 unmapped).
- Each line in a .docx opened read-only by Microsoft Word 16.0.18429 (free edition) in a new hidden COM instance, then exported to PDF (content stream + 225-dpi render compared with the glyph drawn by GDI ExtTextOut ETO_GLYPH_INDEX) and captured as Word's own EMF (EMR_EXTTEXTOUTW plus GDI playback ink).
- RichEdit (msftedit RICHEDIT50W, hidden window), both typed WM_CHAR and the product's RTF via EM_SETTEXTEX.

Gaps I found and filled this session (2026-10-18, 09:40-10:20):
1. The 41 ASCII 0x20-0x7E code points missing from a cmap had never been tested.
   - Which ones: '<' in 21 of the 24 requested families; also ASS7 '%' ':', MAL7/Mal7-00x '>' 'F' 'G' 'H' '[' '{', PUN/PUN7 'x' '{'.
   - How: 24 new docx files, one new hidden Word instance per document (read-only, PDF + EMF; all quit), plus RichEdit typed and RTF.
   - Result: Word draws the real character in Cambria. RichEdit draws the .notdef box, or ॥ in SHREE-BAN and SHREE-ASS: those fonts' usFirstCharIndex is 0x20, so GDI's default character is 0x1F, which they map to ॥.
2. Several step-3 glyph names were wrong at the Bangla family-differing codes, because the 7 composer's meaning follows the 4/5/6 layout there. I fixed them with a rendered check and the groundtruth fontCheck:
   - '@' is the half-ন hook in BAN7, ASS7 and Ban7-00x, not ঃ.
   - U+2013 is the hook in BAN, ASS and Ass7-00x.
   - U+2014 is the subscript ্ন (4/5/6) or a spacing ৺-like sign (7).
   - '%' is a zero-width mark in BAN7.
   - U+0152 is a copy of ব in the 7 fonts.
   - SAN7 'n' is the subscript ्न, not a quote (a composer quirk).
   - 198 glyphs that had no name were checked by eye. 222 more are now named as pieces of composer or table answers.
3. Some RichEdit verdicts for unmapped punctuation in the -00x faces were unclassified; they are the .notdef box, checked by eye.
4. I re-checked the 'known so far' claims:
   - U+0081, U+0090 and U+009E: Word keeps the advance and GDI draws 0 px.
   - U+017E falls back to Cambria and U+20AC to Times New Roman.
   - U+00AD: Word draws it as the font does (blank in most fonts); the PDF export shows '-'.

What Word and RichEdit fail to draw in the requested families:
- C1 code points U+0081, U+008D, U+008F, U+0090, U+009D, U+009E: nothing drawn, advance kept.
- RichEdit only, charset-238 rebinding to Arial: U+0120-012F, U+0152, U+0153, U+0160, U+0161, U+0178, U+0192.
- RichEdit only: U+2219 is moved to Cambria Math.
- U+00AD: PDF artefact in Word; RichEdit hides it where it has ink.
- Code points not in the cmap.

Most important for the Gujarati complaint:
- The shipped guj7 and guj456 tables write every en dash as U+0081 and every em dash as U+0081 U+0081. Word and RichEdit show nothing there, and no other code point reaches that glyph.
- dev7 and dev456 do the same with U+008D.

The per-family JSON files hold, for every code point: cp, gid, word, richedit, sameGlyphAs, sameOutlineAs, draws (with source), tables and alternatives, plus asInput (what the tables write for an ASCII or punctuation input). All scratch files are under the work directory. The repo was not edited, nothing was built, no composer DLL was loaded, and no Word, wordvis or dotnet process of mine is left running.

No table writes U+2219, U+00AD, U+201B or any of the missing ASCII; those reach a legacy run only through FontConverter's pass-through of unmapped input.
